documents.title: Office Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Routine visit. Feels well. Cold snap kept her in, she has been charting the inversions from the porch. No dizziness, no new palpitations, no swelling beyond the usual.
Allergies: sulfa drugs (rash).
Exam: vitals as charted. Heart regular. Lungs clear. Trace ankle edema.
Plan: BMP, Mg, digoxin, INR. Back in 3-4 months.

documents.title: Anticoagulation Note
documents.author: RN
documents.body: INR in therapeutic range. No missed doses, no bleeding or bruising. Continue warfarin 5 mg daily; next INR in 4 weeks.

reports.text: Wide-complex tachycardia at about 150 per minute, consistent with ventricular tachycardia.
Left ventricle mildly dilated with global hypokinesis. LVEF 35%. Right ventricle normal size and function. No significant valve disease. No pericardial effusion.

medications.drug: potassium chloride 20 MEQ Extended Release Oral Tablet

documents.title: Emergency Department Record
documents.author: emergency medicine
documents.body:
Outside emergency department, visit 2025-05-21.

72-year-old woman, past amiodarone and digoxin toxicity, with two hours of palpitations and light-headedness.
Triage: BP 130/85, heart rate 150 and irregular, RR 18.
She says she takes her medicines faithfully, including furosemide, digoxin and warfarin. Home list (outside record): metoprolol succinate 50 mg daily, amiodarone 200 mg daily, benztropine 1 mg BID. Allergy: sulfa drugs (rash).
Labs: potassium 3.0 mEq/L, magnesium 1.2 mg/dL, calcium 9.2 mg/dL, digoxin 1.5 ng/mL, INR 2.5.
ECG: ventricular tachycardia.

Course: sustained wide-complex tachycardia with ongoing light-headedness, managed as unstable. Procedural sedation and synchronized cardioversion, one shock, to sinus rhythm. IV potassium and magnesium replacement. Admitted to cardiology telemetry.

documents.title: Hospital Discharge Summary
documents.author: cardiology
documents.body:
Outside hospital, cardiology service. Admitted 2025-05-21, discharged 2025-05-23.

Diagnosis: ventricular tachycardia, treated with synchronized cardioversion, in the setting of hypokalemia (3.0) and hypomagnesemia (1.2) on loop diuretic.
Course: no recurrence on telemetry after electrolytes were replaced. Echo: LVEF 35%, unchanged. Digoxin level 1.5, within range; digoxin continued. Because the arrhythmia had a reversible cause, an ICD was not recommended at this time.
Discharge medications: potassium chloride 20 mEq daily (new), magnesium oxide 400 mg daily (new), metoprolol succinate 50 mg daily, digoxin 0.125 mg daily, furosemide 40 mg daily, warfarin per INR, benztropine 1 mg BID.
Follow-up: primary care within one week with BMP and magnesium; cardiology in 4 weeks.

documents.title: Post-Hospital Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Hospital follow-up. Admitted 5/21-5/23 after VT with K 3.0 and Mg 1.2; cardioverted in the ED. Now on KCl 20 mEq and magnesium oxide 400 mg daily. No palpitations since. A little sore on the chest where the pads were. Taking everything as listed.
Med reconciliation done with her bottles: metoprolol succinate 50, digoxin 0.125, furosemide 40, warfarin 5, benztropine 1 BID, KCl 20 mEq, Mg oxide 400. The hospital ED list showed amiodarone; she has not taken it since 2021. Allergies: sulfa drugs (rash).
Exam: vitals as charted. Heart regular. Lungs clear. Trace edema.
Labs today: K 4.2, Mg 1.9. INR drawn.
Plan: continue supplements. BMP and Mg again in 2 months. Cardiology 6/19.

documents.title: Cardiology Follow-up Letter
documents.author: cardiology
documents.body:
Outside cardiology, visit 2025-06-19.

Four weeks after VT related to low potassium and magnesium. No recurrence of palpitations or presyncope. Sinus rhythm. Electrolytes normal on your recheck. Allergy: sulfa (rash).
Plan: continue potassium and magnesium supplements with furosemide; keep potassium above 4. No ICD for now. Yearly follow-up, sooner with symptoms.

documents.title: Anticoagulation Note
documents.author: RN
documents.body: INR reviewed, at goal. Pt reports diet unchanged. Continue current dose. Reminder card mailed for next draw.

documents.title: Office Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Summer follow-up. Feels steady. No palpitations since May. Taking the potassium and magnesium; the magnesium loosens her stools a little, tolerable.
Allergies: sulfa drugs (rash).
Exam: vitals as charted. Heart regular. Lungs clear. Trace edema.
Plan: BMP, Mg, INR. Fall vaccines at a nurse visit in October; wellness visit in November.

documents.title: Anticoagulation Note
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Left voicemail: INR fine, keep the same warfarin dose, next check in 4-5 weeks.

documents.title: Nurse Visit
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Flu (high-dose) left deltoid and 2025-26 COVID right deltoid. INR drawn by fingerstick and venous sample sent. No reaction.

documents.title: Annual Wellness Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Annual wellness visit, just turned 73.

Interval: VT in May tied to low potassium and magnesium, cardioverted, now on supplements; no recurrence. Cardiology June, no ICD. Eyes stable after iridotomies and right lens.
Function: independent, drives in daylight. No falls. Still runs the weather class in the fall term.
PHQ-2: 0. Cognition screen normal.
Advance care: proxy on file, reviewed; no changes.
Meds: metoprolol succinate 50, digoxin 0.125, furosemide 40, warfarin 5 per INR, benztropine 1 BID, KCl 20 mEq, Mg oxide 400. Allergies: sulfa drugs (rash).
Exam: vitals as charted. Lungs clear. Heart regular. Trace ankle edema.
Plan: CBC, CMP, TSH, Mg, digoxin, INR. Vaccines up to date. Next visit February.

documents.title: Neurology Follow-up Letter
documents.author: neurology
documents.body:
Outside neurology, visit 2025-12-04.

Parkinson's disease, stable. Mild right-hand rest tremor, unchanged. Gait steady. She continues benztropine 1 mg BID; her eye doctors cleared it after the iridotomies. Allergy: sulfa (rash).
Plan: no change. Return in one year.
